title: Substitution $T\mapsto c^{-1}T^{-1}$ in an alternating product of polynomials with degreewise reciprocity
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], $T$ an indeterminate, $K[T]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and $K(T)$ the field of rational functions [def-weil-rational-function-field]; for $R\in K(T)$ and $u\in K^\times$, $R(uT^{-1})$ denotes the substitution of $uT^{-1}$ for $T$, the involutive $K$-algebra automorphism of $K(T)$ of that definition, and for a polynomial $P\in K[T]$, $P(uT^{-1})$ is its evaluation at $uT^{-1}\in K(T)$. Negative integer exponents denote multiplicative inverses in $K^\times$ or in $K(T)^\times$.

Let $c\in K^\times$ and let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. For every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ let $P_i\in K[T]$ with $P_i(0)=1$ (so $P_i\neq0$), let $b_i\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and let $D_i\in K^\times$. Assume that for every integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$:

1. $b_i=b_{2d-i}$;

2. $D_iD_{2d-i}=c^{b_i}$;

3. $P_{2d-i}(c^{-1}T^{-1})=(-1)^{b_i}\,T^{-b_i}\,D_i^{-1}\,P_i(T)$ in $K(T)$.

Put

$$
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i\in\mathbf Z,\qquad
\Delta=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}\in K^\times,\qquad
Z(T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}\in K(T)^\times.
$$

Then

$$
\text{(a)}\quad \Delta^2=c^{\chi}\ \text{ in }K^\times,
\qquad\qquad
\text{(b)}\quad Z(c^{-1}T^{-1})=(-1)^{\chi}\,T^{\chi}\,\Delta\,Z(T)\ \text{ in }K(T).
$$

Assertion (b) uses only hypotheses 1 and 3; assertion (a) uses only hypotheses 1 and 2.

source.place: ## Proof, step 2, first display and the display for $\Delta^2$: the reindexing of the product $\prod_iP_i(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$ under $T\mapsto q^{-d}T^{-1}$ by $i\mapsto2d-i$ and the computation $\Delta^2=\prod_i(D_iD_{2d-i})^{(-1)^i}=q^{d\chi}$, here stated as a lemma of pure field algebra with $K=\mathbf Q$, $c=q^d$ in the application (slopmaster2: proof of prop:functional-equation, literature/blueprint/slopmaster2/src/version/sketch/01_final_weil_conjectures.tex lines 3523-3551, which states the proposition without a proof).
